questions.question: How does food preservation prevent microbial growth?
questions.solution_html:
• Preservation usually involves preventing the growth of bacteria, fungi (such as yeasts), and other
  • microorganisms, as well as retarding the oxidation of fats which cause rancidity. A number of
  • methods of prevention can be used that can either totally prevent, delay, or otherwise reduce
  • food spoilage.
  • Temperature Control- Refrigeration, Freezing, Heat Treatment: Includes
  • pasteurization and sterilization to kill pathogens. 2. Water Activity Reduction-Dehydration
  • Salting, Sugaring 3. pH Control 4. Chemical Preservatives 5. Modified Atmosphere Packaging
  • (MAP) 6. Biological Control
  • Moisture foods 2) Chilled foods 3) fermented foods
  • Hurdle technology is defined as a technique that combines existing and novel methods for food
  • preservation to improve quality and inhibit microbial growth. State the application in moisture
  • foods, chilled foods and fermented foods
questions.final_answer: foods, chilled foods and fermented foods
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is syruping and brining? How is it done?
questions.solution_html:
• Syruping is a preservation and flavoring technique that involves soaking or cooking fruit in a
  • sugar syrup. It’s used to preserve fruit, candy fruit pieces, or create dessert toppings. Brining is
  • the process of soaking food—usually meat, poultry, or vegetables—in a saltwater solution.
  • It helps retain moisture, improve texture, and enhance

questions.question: List out the advantages & disadvantages of osmotic dehydration.
questions.solution_html:
• List out the advantages and disadvantages of osmotic dehydration
  • Osmotic dehydration is a process where water is partially removed from fruits, vegetables, or
  • other food materials by immersing them in a hypertonic solution (such as sugar or salt solution).
  • It’s often used as a pre-treatment before drying, freezing, or other preservation methods.
  • Aspect Advantages Disadvantages
  • Product Quality Better color, flavor, and nutrients retained Possible solute taste alteration
  • Processing Gentle, low-temperature process Time-consuming
  • Energy Use Reduces drying energy High solute consumption
  • Shelf Life Lower water activity Nutrient leaching possible
  • Environmental Impact — Waste solution disposal issues
questions.final_answer: Environmental Impact — Waste solution disposal issues
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write short notes on Plate freezing Immersion freezing
questions.solution_html:
• Plate freezing is a method used to freeze food products quickly and efficiently. It involves
  • placing food items between two metal plates that are cooled to low temperatures. Immersion
  • freezing is a process in which ice forms within a supercooled liquid due to the presence of solid
  • particles that act as nucleation sites.
questions.final_answer: particles that act as nucleation sites
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write a brief note on radappertization, radurization and radicidation. / Enumerate the preservation methods used in the killing of
questions.solution_html:
• Radappertization- A high-dose irradiation process (usually 30–40 kGy) used to achieve
  • commercial sterility of food.
  • Radurization: A pasteurization-level irradiation process (typically 0.75–10 kGy).
  • Radicidation : An irradiation process (around 2–8 kGy) aimed at destroying specific non
  • spore-forming pathogenic microorganisms.
questions.final_answer: spore-forming pathogenic microorganisms
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain in detail on flash 18 process.
questions.solution_html:
• Flash 18 process is a continuous canning/sterilisation method in which the product is brought up
  • to sterilising temperature prior to filling, and the filling and sealing are done under pressure (≈ 18
  • psi above atmospheric) so that the product remains above its normal boiling point. This enables
  • sterilisation at higher temperature and shorter time, improving product quality
questions.final_answer: sterilisation at higher temperature and shorter time, improving product quality
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What do you mean by exhausting of cans? List the methods and advantages of exhausting.
questions.solution_html:
• Exhausting is a unit operation in which practically all the air is removed from the contents of
  • the can before sealing.
  • Methods of exhausting- Heat, steam, cold and mechanical exhausting
  • Adavantages of exhausting –Prevents oxidation of food components, Reduce corrosion of metal
  • cans, Ensure formation of proper vacuum
questions.final_answer: cans, Ensure formation of proper vacuum

questions.question: / irradiation in food industry.
questions.solution_html:
• Industry
  •  Irradiation is the process by which an object is exposed to radiation. An irradiator is a device
  • used to expose an object to radiation, most often gamma radiation, for a variety of purposes.
  • Food irradiation has various practical applications, including sprout inhibition in tubers and
  • bulbs, delay in fruit ripening, and decontamination of spices and other food products.
questions.final_answer: bulbs, delay in fruit ripening, and decontamination of spices and other food products
